topic: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness

audits.title: Adequacy of clinical information in X-ray referrals for traumatic ankle injury with reference to the Ottawa Ankle Rules-a retrospective clinical audit.
audits.standard: Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria documented on adult ankle X-ray referrals
audits.setting: Emergency department, Flinders Medical Centre (tertiary hospital), South Australia

cycle1.result: 163/262 referrals met Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria; 99 of 262 (38%) did not. Compliance by profession: physiotherapists 77.3%, nurses 65.4%, consultants 61.5%, registrars/MOs/interns 54.8%. Overall sensitivity 0.59 and specificity 0.37.

audits.other_findings: Registrars/MOs/interns were 2.5 times more likely than physiotherapists to refer despite not meeting the rules (OR 2.48, p = 0.026). Duration of injury was not specified on 76.3% of referrals.
audits.citation: Gomes YE, Chau M, Banwell HA, Davies J, Causby RS. Adequacy of clinical information in X-ray referrals for traumatic ankle injury with reference to the Ottawa Ankle Rules-a retrospective clinical audit. PeerJ. 2020;8:e10152. doi:10.7717/peerj.10152. PMID: 33083152.

audits.title: Evaluating Compliance With the Ottawa Rules: A Retrospective Clinical Audit at a District General Hospital in the UK.
audits.standard: Ottawa Ankle and Knee Rules (incorporated in NICE guidance) for requesting X-rays
audits.setting: Emergency department and urgent treatment centre, Lincoln County Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 59.5%; knee X-rays 74.6% (n=182); ankle X-rays 33.1% (n=46). Positivity 18.0% knee and 32.0% ankle.

audits.intervention: Educational session, leaflets, posters in ED and UTC and emails to clinicians (August 2023).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 85% (221/260); knee X-rays 89.9% (152); ankle X-rays 75.8% (69). Positivity 18.9% knee and 44.0% ankle.

audits.other_findings: Compliance was much lower for patients under 55 (22.5% in cycle 1, 69.9% in cycle 2). Compliance was judged from radiology requests only.
audits.citation: Dalla Ali S, Alhiraki OA, Naeem T. Evaluating Compliance With the Ottawa Rules: A Retrospective Clinical Audit at a District General Hospital in the UK. Cureus. 2024;16(7):e65115. doi:10.7759/cureus.65115. PMID: 39171035.

audits.title: Assessing Compliance With Ottawa Foot and Ankle Rules in the Emergency Department: A Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: ED clerking documentation and X-ray request clinical details should contain the relevant Ottawa Ankle or Foot Rule criteria in all cases (NICE; RCR/IR(ME)R 2017)
audits.setting: Emergency department, South London district general hospital

cycle1.result: 100 ankle and 100 foot X-ray requests. Ankle: documentation compliance 74%, X-ray request compliance 43%. Foot: documentation compliance 48%, X-ray request compliance 32%.

audits.intervention: First-cycle results distributed and an Ottawa rules handout given to ED staff, plus a small-group teaching session for ED junior doctors on assessing, documenting and requesting foot and ankle X-rays (mid-April 2024)

cycle2.result: Ankle: documentation 87% (p<.05), X-ray request 57% (p<.05). Foot: documentation 78% (p<.001 in abstract; p<.0001 in results), X-ray request 54% (p<.01).

audits.other_findings: Ankle fracture rate rose from 17% to 22% (p=.37) and midfoot fracture rate stayed at 15%. Foot compliance stayed lower than ankle compliance in both cycles; authors suggest an electronic X-ray request template.
audits.citation: Wallace W, Limaye N, Rao C, Menon S, Ratcliffe G, Mostafa A, et al.. Assessing Compliance With Ottawa Foot and Ankle Rules in the Emergency Department: A Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(5):e84908. doi:10.7759/cureus.84908. PMID: 40575204.

audits.title: Evaluating the Impact of Audits and Re-audits on Adherence to the Ottawa Knee Rules in a High-Volume UK Trauma Centre.
audits.standard: Ottawa Knee Rules (endorsed by NICE and RCR iRefer) documented in knee radiograph requests; target 100%
audits.setting: Emergency department and orthopaedic referrers, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (high-volume trauma centre)

cycle1.result: At least one OKR criterion documented 41%; age >=55 52%; fibular head tenderness 3%; isolated patellar tenderness 13%; inability to flex to 90 degrees 3%; inability to bear weight 14%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 35.7%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 52.4%.

audits.intervention: Posters and leaflets in clinical areas, presentations at departmental meetings, formal and informal teaching, and emails summarising the rules.

cycle2.result: At least one OKR criterion 91% (p<0.01); age 62%; fibular head tenderness 68%; patellar tenderness 72%; inability to flex 65%; inability to bear weight 57%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 92.9%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 88.2%.

audits.other_findings: 9% of cycle 2 referrals still lacked adequate documentation; authors suggest OKR prompts in the electronic request system.
audits.citation: Ahmed H, Gilani A, Mazhar F, Rizwan M, Azeem A, Rehman A. Evaluating the Impact of Audits and Re-audits on Adherence to the Ottawa Knee Rules in a High-Volume UK Trauma Centre. Cureus. 2025;17(7):e87426. doi:10.7759/cureus.87426. PMID: 40772178.

audits.title: Audit of Ottawa Knee Rules Compliance in the Emergency Department: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study at a General Hospital.
audits.standard: RCR iRefer guidelines: ≥95% of knee radiographs requested in accordance with Ottawa Knee Rules; ≥95% of requests documenting an OKR indication; unnecessary imaging ≤10%
audits.setting: Emergency department, St. Luke's General Hospital, Kilkenny (general hospital)

cycle1.result: OKR compliance 50 (72.5%); non-compliant requests 19 (27.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 23 (32.9%); negative X-rays 37 (52.9%)

audits.intervention: Interactive teaching session for ED clinicians, OKR leaflets distributed and emailed, and posters in ED clinical areas and beside imaging request stations

cycle2.result: OKR compliance 66 (83.5%) (χ²=2.05, p=0.15); non-compliant requests 13 (16.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 44 (55.7%) (p=0.01); negative X-rays 30 (38.0%) (p=0.08)

audits.other_findings: Compliance remained below the 95% target. Estimated radiographer time saved was about 60-90 minutes per cycle.
audits.citation: Rehman A, Javed MA. Audit of Ottawa Knee Rules Compliance in the Emergency Department: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study at a General Hospital. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e95532. doi:10.7759/cureus.95532. PMID: 41311778.

audits.title: Traumatic Ankle Injuries in the Emergency Department: Evaluating the Adequacy of Clinical Documentation With Reference to the Ottawa Ankle Rules.
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists: 100% of ankle plain-film requests for trauma should reference the Ottawa Ankle Rules
audits.setting: Emergency department, Newham University Hospital (district general hospital, East London)

cycle1.result: 37/100 (37%) requests referenced the OAR. 21 (21%) fractures; 13 (61.9%) of these requests documented the OAR and 8 (38.1%) did not (P = 0.011).

audits.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance meetings; focused education sessions for front-line clinicians and targeted briefings for radiographers who vet X-ray requests.

cycle2.result: 51/100 (51%) requests referenced the OAR (P = 0.046). 31 (31%) fractures; 26 (83.9%) had OAR documented and 5 (16.1%) did not (P < 0.001).

audits.other_findings: Compliance remained well below the 100% RCR target. Authors suggest electronic OAR prompts in request systems and induction teaching for rotating doctors.
audits.citation: Anwar A, Ali MH, Ali H, Anwar W, Baalawi MS. Traumatic Ankle Injuries in the Emergency Department: Evaluating the Adequacy of Clinical Documentation With Reference to the Ottawa Ankle Rules. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e95645. doi:10.7759/cureus.95645. PMID: 41322931.

audits.title: Overuse of knee ultrasound in acute knee injury pathways in primary care: a quality improvement report.
audits.standard: ACC imaging guidelines for knee ultrasound
audits.setting: Sport and exercise physician-led Acute Knee Clinic, primary care

cycle1.result: 9.8% had knee ultrasound before specialist review; only one scan met ACC criteria; 80% requested by physiotherapists (P = 0.015).

audits.other_findings: 21% had not received a knee X-ray; trend to longer time to MRI with ultrasound (P = 0.173).
audits.citation: Krishna S, Young S, Fulcher M. Overuse of knee ultrasound in acute knee injury pathways in primary care: a quality improvement report. J Prim Health Care. 2026. doi:10.1071/hc26033. PMID: 42098586.

audits.title: An audit of knee radiographs performed for general practitioners.
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidelines for knee radiography (locking or restricted movement)
audits.setting: Department of Radiology, Leicester Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Only 50% within RCR guidelines; 90% normal or degenerative; 87% led to no significant change in management.

cycle2.result: Referral rate for knee radiographs unchanged.

audits.other_findings: In 42% requests were to confirm expected degeneration and in 30% patient pressure was significant.
audits.citation: Morgan B, Mullick S, Harper WM, Finlay DB. An audit of knee radiographs performed for general practitioners. Br J Radiol. 1997;70:256-260. doi:10.1259/bjr.70.831.9166050. PMID: 9166050.

audits.title: Plain radiography of the lumbosacral spine. An audit of referrals from general practitioners.
audits.standard: Norwegian and British referral guides for lumbosacral spine radiography
audits.setting: Radiologic Section, University Hospital, Bergen; GP referrals

cycle1.result: 24% (37%) conformed to the Norwegian (British) guide, 34% (46%) did not conform and 42% (18%) were uncertain.

audits.other_findings: Only 4 of 182 non-conforming examinations showed potentially important findings.
audits.citation: Espeland A, Albrektsen G, Larsen JL. Plain radiography of the lumbosacral spine. An audit of referrals from general practitioners. Acta Radiol. 1999;40(1):52-59. doi:10.1080/02841859909174403. PMID: 9973903.
